Concrete staging repro of this staleness seam, 2026-08-22 (cloud#1584): confirm-replay issued two sequential `publishPackageDrafts` calls in one turn — dataset `k9qk_task_stats` published → `active`; the dashboard referencing it was **refused** moments later with `[widget-dataset-unknown]` and a hint listing only `sys_*` datasets, i.e. the gate's resolution universe did not include an already-active same-package row. The byte-identical draft published cleanly ~10 minutes later once the kernel had rebuilt. #10389 covers same-batch pending declarations; this is the cross-call case — the universe appears kernel-snapshot-fed rather than `sys_metadata`-fed, so every within-turn sequential publish races the async rebuild that this issue's `metadata:reloaded` broadcast is about.

Second concrete repro of the ledger split, now cross-surface (cloud#1593, staging 2026-08-22): a `mode='draft'` save lands in `sys_metadata` (single-read `?state=draft` returns it; `publishPackageDrafts` collects and publishes it, `publishedCount:1`) while `GET /meta/_drafts` returns `{"drafts":[]}` throughout — list and publisher disagree about what is pending. Every ambient 「未发布改动」 surface counts via the list, so users see 0 pending while the publisher would publish 1. Also: the draft-save did not inherit `package_id` from the active row it overlays (orphan until manually bound).
